title: three lifecycles on one board family: the PSP blobs, the SMM armor, and a security patch

psp_chronology.note: PSP/BIOS directory blob fingerprints across the nine dated PRIME rungs (ring-13 machinery, fletcher-validated)
psp_chronology.reading: the 3802 event is cross-confirmed: 42/50 blob types move at 3802 — the release where the SMM armor appears — while 3810 moves 7/50 (same AGESA 1.2.0.7, a quiet maintenance release); every later transition churns 28-43/50; ABL0/ABL6/APCB/key/policy blobs move at almost every rung

smm_anatomy.note: the armor modules opened: size, DEPEX, vocabulary, body identity across the rungs
smm_anatomy.reading: SbRomArmorSmm is ONE body across 8 rungs (4.5 years, byte-identical); PrepareWhiteListSmm carries the literal string 'AMD rom armor' plus an SPI flash chip database (ADESTO/AMIC/ATMEL/MXIC...); the SMM census grows 106->109 at 3802 then settles at 107 after the legacy retirement

patch_lens.note: Gigabyte F65 -> F67c (2026-04 -> 2026-08), the update carrying CVE-2026-6726/6727, diffed at FFS-body granularity with the ring-15 machinery
patch_lens.reading: a vendor security patch is a platform rebuild, not a patch: 81.9 % of the GUID set changes in four months (410/503 modules, 107 of them SMM) — the mirror image of the ring-15 surgical story (ASUS AcpiTableDxe, 9 bytes); the patch also rides an AGESA bump (1.2.0.B -> 1.2.0.12); isolation of the CVE fix inside this churn is impossible at FFS granularity

honesty: body-hash identity sees REBUILDS as changes: the Gigabyte churn figure includes toolchain noise; the reading is about release PHILOSOPHY, not 410 semantic fixes

F65 was re-fetched 2026-09-12 from the official CDN at the listing's canonical URL (board id 8a16bg04) after the sandbox's old 'f65 zip' proved to be a 196-byte 404 page; zip sha256_16 9cbfd8f4bd7f3ff9
the AGESA ladder is board-family timing, not an industry clock: Gigabyte shipped 1.2.0.B (ASUS 2024-01) in April 2026
PSP type names come from psptool 3.6 tables (runtime import, GPL-3.0, PSPTool project); semantics of some types remain opaque
